Description.Title: Escherichia coli isolated from wastewater samples of Chittagong city BCSIR_EC_C6S6_2019_03_10

Comment.Paragraph: Multidrug resistance has become a crucial problem in todays world. E. coli are Gram negative, rod shaped bacteria of coliform group which have been found to be resistant to three or more major classes of antibiotics hence multidrug resistant. In this project, wastewater samples were collected from the different locations of Chittagong city of Bangladesh and multidrug resistant E. coli were isolated. The genome sequencing of multidrug resistant E. coli will provide us valuable information on genome organization, evolutionary divergence, conservation and overall endemic diversity. The aim of this project is to identify resistant genes related to antibiotic resistance that will help us to know the molecular mechanisms of multidrug resistance.

Comment.Paragraph: This sample represents an Escherichia coli isolate recovered from cattle feces collected in Mymensingh, Bangladesh. The isolate was obtained during a study investigating the genomic characteristics, antimicrobial resistance determinants, and virulence-associated genes of animal-derived E. coli. Whole-genome sequencing was performed to characterize its genomic features and assess its potential public health significance.
